stem:
Ishaan checks which expressions must always be even when the letter-numbers are integers. He compares $4m + 2q$ with $x^{2} + 2$.

Which two claims are correct?

options.text: $4m + 2q$ is always even, because $4m + 2q = 2(2m + q)$ for every integer $m$ and $q$.
$x^{2} + 2$ is always even, because the added constant $2$ is even.
$x^{2} + 2$ is not always even: when $x$ is odd, $x^{2}$ is odd, so $x^{2} + 2$ is odd.
Integer values of the letters are what the even-or-odd conclusion creates.

teacher.key_rationale: 4m+2q factors as 2(2m+q), so it is always even for integers. x^2+2 fails when x is odd. Claiming x^2+2 is always even from the constant alone overreaches; saying integers are created by the parity conclusion reverses the relation.
